wb_handover: Mobile data stays ready while the screen is on, which uses a little more battery

athena_service.name: Athena Background Killer
athena_service.desc: OxygenOS has its own background app killer - com.oplus.athena - and AthenaService is the part that decides what to kill. It is why a messenger left in the background stops delivering notifications until you reopen it, which no amount of battery whitelisting fixes because it is not Android's Doze doing it. Off disables that one component; the rest of the package keeps running, so thermal reporting and the settings panels are unaffected. Fully reversible: the previous state is recorded before anything changes and put back when you set this to stock or remove the module. Expect more RAM in use and slightly more drain - that is what keeping apps alive costs.

descOpt.stock: OxygenOS keeps killing background apps as it normally does.
descOpt.off: AthenaService is disabled, so apps stay alive and keep notifying. Expect more RAM used and slightly more drain.

descOpt.stock: Android's own timing: idle begins 30 minutes after the screen goes off.
descOpt.night: Only during your learned sleep window. Daytime behaviour is untouched.
descOpt.moderate: Idle after 5 minutes. The change most people want.
descOpt.aggressive: Idle after 2 minutes, plus shorter sensing and locating windows. Apps that poll on their own can be late; high-priority push still arrives.

descOpt.off: Nothing is frozen. Play services behave as shipped.
descOpt.safe: Telemetry and reporting components only. Push, sign-in and payments keep working.
descOpt.more: Adds ads and measurement components. Reversible, but check anything you depend on.

gms_freeze.desc: Disables individual Google Play services components. Levels are cumulative. SAFE: telemetry, stats and analytics - nothing the phone needs. MORE: adds the ad identifier, location reporting and the backup scheduler. MAX: adds Icing indexing and background Fitness recording. THE COST OF MAX: in-app and system search will miss some results, and steps are not counted in the background. Push notifications are untouched at every level. Everything is restored by switching to off - each component's original state is recorded.

descOpt.stock: Play services schedule background work as they like.
descOpt.strict: Noticeably fewer. Some sync may be delayed.

descOpt.stock: Android's own limit applies - background child processes get killed.
descOpt.relaxed: No limit. Terminal sessions and background compiles survive.
descOpt.strict: Limit of 32. Fewer background processes than stock allows.

descOpt.0: Extreme: cuts device logging as far as it goes. Saves writes and wakeups, and makes almost any bug report from this phone useless.
descOpt.1: Normal. Significant events only - what the module has always done.
descOpt.2: Detailed: adds learner updates and screen transitions. Turn this on before sending a battery log.
descOpt.3: Verbose. Fills the log fast; only while reproducing something.
descOpt.stock: ASB does not touch the device's logging at all.
This device's own trip point, read from its CPU thermal zone at boot.
descOpt.smart: Starts from that point and nudges it up when sessions heat quickly.
descOpt.manual: Exactly the temperature on the slider below. Nothing moves it.

descOpt.auto: Leave the system's own effect level alone.
descOpt.stock: Normal effects, as the device shipped.
descOpt.flat: Simplified. Recents becomes a plain list and OxygenOS hides the Cards/Simple selector entirely. OnePlus 15 only.

descOpt.auto: Smart: ASB measures the link and sizes the initial window for it.
descOpt.off: Stock. The route keeps the values Android set.
descOpt.aggressive: Largest window. Best on a fast, stable link; can cost retransmits on a weak one.

descOpt.auto: Hands off - whatever the ROM chose stays.
descOpt.on: Hardware encoding. Less battery, and usually what the phone ships with.
descOpt.off: CPU encoding. Needed for some equaliser apps to see the stream at all.

net_rps.name: Spread Network Load
net_rps.desc: Which cores handle incoming network packets. Stock leaves every packet on the one core the interrupt landed on, which caps throughput on fast WiFi and pins that core high. Little spreads the work across the efficiency cluster; all uses every core. Waking a second core costs a little CPU, so this earns its keep on a fast link and loses on a slow one. Applies to Wi-Fi only: mobile data is left to the phone's own hardware distribution, which a manual mask can only slow down.

descOpt.stock: Every packet stays on the core its interrupt landed on - Android's own behaviour.
descOpt.little: Spread across the efficiency cluster. The safer of the two.
descOpt.all: Every core. Best throughput on fast WiFi, most CPU woken.

net_txqueue.name: Transmit Queue
net_txqueue.desc: How many packets may wait to be sent. The stock 1000 is a wired-Ethernet default from the 1990s that survived into wireless drivers; on a link as variable as WiFi a deep queue mostly adds latency under load rather than throughput. If uploads feel slower, go back to stock.

descOpt.short: 256. Less delay under load, same throughput on most links.
descOpt.shorter: 128. Lowest latency; can cost throughput on a very fast link.

night_modem_idle.name: Quiet Radio at Night
night_modem_idle.desc: Lets the modem settle during the hours the learner worked out from your own nights. A night capture showed the CPU was woken not by apps but by the network path: over a hundred resumes from IPA and rmnet. This stretches keepalive sixfold AND gates data-path wakeups at the rmnet level - top and bottom of the stack together. THE COST: a push notification may arrive at the next wake rather than instantly. Calls and SMS travel the modem's own channel and are untouched; radio power and airplane mode are never altered. Every change is recorded and restored on disable or uninstall.

gnss_trim.name: Trim Background GPS
gnss_trim.desc:
GPS is one of the most expensive things a phone can do, and Android reports how much of it happens in CACHED processes - apps that are closed and doing nothing you asked for.

In one field capture that was 53 of 56 mAh of GPS drain.

When on, a user-installed app still holding location while its process is cached and the screen is off is limited to coarse accuracy. It gets full precision back the moment you open it.

Never touched: maps and navigation, fitness and route tracking, emergency and find-my apps, and anything in the foreground.

smart_media_guard.name: Smart Media Guard
smart_media_guard.desc: Optional, Smart-only protection for a narrow case: a known video, feed or browser app stays game-like CPU + GPU heavy for a full minute while you use it on battery. ASB then keeps only the effective GPU ceiling at the existing 70% media envelope. It never limits a known game, an unknown app, charging, thermal protection, CPU ceilings or frequency floors. Start with the 12-hour trial; turn it off if a high-refresh stream stutters.

radio_policy_enable.name: Cellular / radio controls
radio_policy_enable.desc: Independent master for ASB modem controls. OFF is the default: choosing any power profile leaves Android’s mobile-data context and TCP keepalive settings untouched. This is the recommended setting on WiFi-only or no-SIM devices. Turn it on only if this phone uses a SIM/eSIM and you deliberately want ASB’s separate radio options below. Turning it off immediately restores the Android values recorded before ASB changed them; it never changes airplane mode, carrier selection, roaming, preferred network type, Bluetooth or audio.

bt_link_stability.name: Bluetooth Link Stability
bt_link_stability.desc:
For phones where Bluetooth headphones disconnect on their own during playback. Most devices never do this, so it is off by default.

On stable, Wi-Fi stops scanning for new networks while audio is playing: the 2.4 GHz band and Bluetooth share one antenna, and a scan sweeps the whole band - a stream that misses its slot disconnects.

The cost is that new Wi-Fi networks appear more slowly. Nothing else changes.

No codec is forced.

BG_TRIM_LEVEL.desc:
How hard to limit background apps.

off - do not touch them at all: Android alone decides. Pick this if you want ASB for CPU and thermals and are happy with how background apps behave.

safe - moderate standby buckets for apps you have not opened in a while. Notifications still arrive, nothing freezes.

aggressive - stronger: background apps may lose state and wake less often. Authenticators, the dialer and the Bluetooth stack are protected at every level.

Switching to off returns every app to the bucket it had before ASB moved it.

Heavy apps (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok…) are moved to "rare" only when Android itself says they are not in daily use; an app you open every day is left alone.

Aggressive adds a re-check every 6 hours, a memory ceiling for heavy apps and a memory trim of idle heavy apps while the screen is off. Package disabling and vendor service stops happen only with the explicit opt-in file /data/adb/asb/allow_disruptive_bg_trim.

mglru_hold.name: Keep Apps In Memory
mglru_hold.desc: Protects the working set from reclaim so the foreground app is not evicted under memory pressure and rebuilt when you return to it. HOLD: 1 second of protection. AGGRESSIVE: 2 seconds - apps survive longer, less free RAM. Only has an effect on kernels with MGLRU; elsewhere the tweak does nothing.

net_wifi_leave.name: Leave Bad Wi-Fi
net_wifi_leave.desc: Wi-Fi that is connected but not working keeps the phone retrying instead of switching to mobile. Each rung leaves sooner: weak signal, then a link carrying no traffic, then handing over without waiting. How it leaves: with the screen on, ASB switches Wi-Fi off for 30 s and back on; if it keeps rejoining the same weak network, the pause doubles up to 5 min. Works without Cellular controls.

descOpt.off: Stock: Wi-Fi is released only when the link actually drops.
descOpt.weak: Leave when the signal falls below -80 dBm.
descOpt.unusable: The above, plus leave a link that is connected but carries no traffic.
descOpt.aggressive: The above, plus hand over to mobile without waiting for the link to fail.

descOpt.0: No background scanning. Networks appear only when you open Wi-Fi settings.
descOpt.1: Every 10 minutes. Noticeably less radio time on a phone that stays in one place.
descOpt.3: Every 2 minutes. Faster to spot a network you walk into.

wifi_powersave.name: WiFi Power Save

descOpt.off: Radio stays fully awake - the shipped behaviour.
descOpt.screen_off: Sleep the radio between beacons while the display is off.
descOpt.always: Keep power save on at all times, screen up or down.

wifi_powersave.desc: Lets the Wi-Fi radio doze between packets. "Screen off" is the safe choice: latency only rises while you are not looking. "Always" saves more but can add a fraction of a second to games and voice calls over Wi-Fi.

ltpo_force.name: Force LTPO Refresh
ltpo_force.desc:
LTPO panels can fall to their lowest refresh rate when nothing on the screen moves; OxygenOS ships parts of that path switched off. This patch takes your device's OWN refresh-rate table (oplus_vrr_config.json), enables every panel power-saving switch the OEM left disabled (ADFR, PDFR, refresh-rate director, histogram backlight control and more), and additionally turns OFF the display stack's own telemetry (VRR info records, histogram sampling, big-data and shader cache-miss upload) - free battery with zero impact on the picture. Nothing is copied from another model, and the stock file itself is never modified.

The patch is prepared while the module installs, and this switch decides whether it is applied: off by default, and turning it on takes effect after a reboot. If the installer found no refresh-rate table on your device, or nothing left to improve in it, the switch does nothing - the install log and the status badge say which.

On a table the OEM already ships fully enabled (OnePlus 15 is one) the patch still earns its keep: an identical copy is bound with only the telemetry switches cut.

The switch also opens the Android side of the range, and that part applies at once, without a reboot: no refresh floor, and the peak set to the highest mode this panel reports (165 Hz on the OnePlus 15). The low end - the panel's own idle rates below 60 Hz - is the table's job, because Android does not list those rates at all. What was set before is recorded and restored when you switch off. The OEM's own cap on the render rate (90 Hz on some builds) is left alone.

mmfeed_off.name: Multimedia Telemetry Off
mmfeed_off.desc:
OxygenOS runs a multimedia feedback collector: audio, video and display diag events with log dumps and uploads, opened by Multimedia_Feedback_List.xml. This patch takes your device's OWN copy of that file, flips only its isOpen switch to false, and binds the result over the stock file - nothing is copied from another model, and the stock file itself is never modified.

The patch is prepared while the module installs, and this switch decides whether it is applied: off by default, and turning it on takes effect after a reboot. If the installer found no such file on your device, or the OEM already ships it closed, this switch does nothing - the status badge says which.

Less event logging and fewer dumps means free battery and less I/O; audio and video themselves are untouched.

net_screen_off_lte.name: LTE While Screen Off
net_screen_off_lte.desc: After the screen has been off for 90 seconds, drops the 5G leg and keeps data on LTE; 5G comes back the moment the screen turns on. 5G NSA keeps two radios busy at once, while listening to a stream with the screen dark needs far less than LTE alone carries. Never acts during a call. Off by default: changing the allowed network types re-registers the data link, which takes a few seconds on some ROMs. If the ROM does not accept the change, the module restores the original value and stops trying. A download keeps 5G: a check at 3 Mbit/s or more is a transfer, not a stream - LTE is not chosen then, and if LTE is already on, 5G comes back for at least 10 minutes.

net_lte_light.name: 5G Only When Needed
net_lte_light.desc: With the screen on: after 3 minutes of light mobile traffic (under 2 Mbit/s - feeds, music) drops the 5G leg and stays on LTE, which carries that easily. A download brings 5G back within about 20 seconds (3 Mbit/s or more in two 10-second checks in a row, or one check over 12 Mbit/s) and keeps it for 10 minutes. 5G NSA keeps two radios busy for a trickle of data. Never during a call, tethering or a game, never on Wi-Fi. Off by default: each switch re-registers the data link for a second or two.

descOpt.keep: ASB does not touch LSPosed's settings.
descOpt.off: LSPosed's verbose log off from the next boot; old verbose logs deleted now.

Exempt - Android itself has this app exempt: you allowed it (Battery > Unrestricted) or the app asked for it. ASB has not touched it.
Exempt via ASB - Android had no exemption for it; ASB gave one because you ticked the app. Untick it and ASB takes it back.
Trimmed by ASB - the app was exempt and ASB took the exemption away. Tick it and the exemption comes back.
Never trimmed - kept by ASB's own rules: authenticators, Bluetooth, watches and bands, caller ID.
Ticked - your list: ASB never trims these apps and keeps them exempt.
Trimmed - the apps ASB has taken the exemption from right now. With Deep Sleep on night this list fills only inside the sleep window.

prof_performance_desc: Top clocks for games and heavy apps
lvi_cpu: Temperature of the CPU cores. ASB steers by one core sensor that it checks against its neighbours, so a stuck zone is never trusted; in Stock it is the hottest core. Up to about 45 °C is cool, short spikes when an app opens are normal, and throttling starts around 60 °C held for a while.
lvi_skin: Temperature of the shell - what your hand feels. It moves slowly and trails the CPU by minutes. Up to about 38 °C feels neutral, above about 42 °C the phone feels warm, and around 45 °C the system starts holding performance back.
lvi_board: Temperature of the main board under the shell. It sits between the CPU and the shell and shows heat soaking into the phone: after a game or a long charge it stays high even when the CPU has already cooled.
lvi_fsm: What ASB thinks the phone is doing: DEEP_IDLE - asleep with the screen off, LIGHT_IDLE - screen on with nothing to do, MODERATE - ordinary use, HEAVY - an app launch or a heavy page, SUSTAINED - long heavy work with heat, GAMING - a game. Each state has its own frequency ceilings.
lvi_gpu: How busy the graphics processor is, as a share of time. Scrolling and video sit around 5-30%, games at 50-100%. A game state is entered only when the load stays high, not on a single spike.
lvi_headroom: How much of the CPU hardware maximum the current ceilings allow, on the most limited cluster. 100% means nothing holds the CPU back. A low figure on a cool phone is a profile or vendor limit, not heat.
lvi_capsrc: Who set the CPU frequency ceiling right now: “ASB” - the profile and Smart; “Vendor” - the OnePlus thermal or performance service; “Thermal” - a thermal overlay; “Shell” - the profile script, for a few seconds after a switch until the governor takes over again. When the vendor holds a lower ceiling ASB leaves it alone rather than fighting it.
lvi_clamps: How often the vendor service pushed the ceiling below what ASB asked for: in the last hour, and since ASB started. A few an hour is normal; dozens mean a hot phone or an aggressive vendor mode.
lvi_learner: How many stretches of use (“{ses}” on the tile) Smart has learned from, across all twelve slots. Every 20 minutes of use and every night adds one. The more there are, the more Smart decides from measurements of your phone instead of defaults.
lvi_slot: Smart splits the day into six parts - {dp0} 0–6, {dp1} 6–9, {dp2} 9–12, {dp3} 12–17, {dp4} 17–21, {dp5} 21–24 - kept apart for weekdays (“{wd}”) and weekends (“{we}”): twelve slots, each with its own measurements. This is the slot the phone is in now. What a workday morning costs is not spent on a Sunday morning.
lvi_conf: How much Smart trusts what it has measured for this slot. The figure grows with every stretch of use; while it is low, Smart leans on neighbouring slots and safe defaults instead of guessing from a handful of samples.
lvi_alpha: How far the current policy leans from {bal} toward {bat}, in percent, learned from what this slot usually costs. 0% is {bal} behaviour; higher values hold the phone back more to save charge. Heat, a game or a camera session pushes it back down on its own.
lvi_apphint: What the foreground load looks like right now: “{app0}”, “{app1}”, “{app2}”, “{app3}” or “{app4}”. Smart reads it from the app in front and the load it creates, and gives games and heavy work more frequency headroom than a messenger.
lvi_basis: What steers Smart right now. Usually the records for the situation you are in: “{rec}” - a setting cheaper than the original one by the share shown was found, checked by pairs of measurements; “{rok}” - the original setting is already the best; “{trial}” - a neighbouring setting is being tried, pairs done of pairs needed. “{smt}” / “{smo}” - this app’s smoothness is being tested, or the extra headroom that helped it is kept. While this time slot has little history, the tile shows where Smart borrows from: “{fb1}”, “{fb2}”, “{fb3}”, “{fb4}”. Protection comes first: “{cold}”, “{lowb}”, “{brief}”, “{night}”, “{guard}”. Below: the records of every situation.
lvi_slotheat: Not the temperature now - how warm this slot usually runs. Smart remembers the CPU peak of every stretch of use in each slot and compares this slot with the phone’s own norm, the middle of all its slots: “{hcool}”, “{hnorm}” or “{hwarm}”. A slot that usually runs warm gets slightly gentler ceilings in advance, before the phone heats up; one that runs cool gets a little headroom back.
lvi_trend: Where the phone’s temperature is heading: “{up}”, “{fl}” or “{dn}”. A warming trend makes Smart back off before a hard thermal limit is reached; cooling gives the headroom back. Right after a profile switch the trend stays muted for two minutes, so a stale reading cannot steer the new profile.
lvi_lpm: The modem’s power mode, read from the governor’s own state file: “{lnormal}” follows the profile; “{lsave}” lets the radio idle with stretched keepalives (screen off or the {bat} profile); “{lfast}” keeps latency low for games and downloads; “{lnight}” stretches idling further inside the night window Smart learned from your routine.
lvi_cpuceil: How much of the hardware maximum the ROM lets the CPU reach right now, on the most limited cluster. In Stock ASB sets no ceilings, so anything under 100% here comes from the OnePlus thermal or performance service.
lvi_gpuclk: The graphics clock at this moment. It drops to the minimum when nothing is drawn and climbs with load; in Stock ASB does not touch it.
lvi_battemp: Battery temperature. Above about 40 °C charging slows down and the battery ages faster; above about 45 °C the system limits performance to protect it.
lvi_zram: Compressed memory (zRAM) in use. Android packs apps you have not used for a while here instead of closing them. Several GB is normal with many apps open; it costs CPU time only when an app is unpacked again.
lvi_learnpause: In Stock Smart neither learns nor decides - the ASB frequency policy is off. Everything it has learned is kept and is used again as soon as you switch back to Smart.
eta_meter_tip: Estimate: nothing measured since the governor started - based on the screen-on drain ASB measured earlier in this profile, over %s min.
lvi_sdrain: The current flowing out of the battery right now, read straight from the battery driver. It jumps with every tap and falls when the screen goes off - the hourly drain with the screen on and off is in the two tiles above. Below: this current as an hourly rate.
lvi_strend: Where the CPU temperature is heading, from ROM readings every 10 seconds over the last two minutes: “{up}”, “{fl}” or “{dn}”. In {stock} nothing in ASB reacts to it; it shows what the phone’s own thermal management is working against. For the first half-minute after Monitor opens it is still measuring (…).
lvi_slpm: Whether the ROM keeps mobile data up while Wi-Fi is connected (the “mobile data always active” developer setting): “{lfast}” - kept up, a faster handover for a little more drain; “{lnormal}” - the ROM’s default. In {stock} ASB applies no modem policy; this is the ROM’s own setting.
lvi_sram: Memory available to apps right now without closing anything, next to the phone’s total. Android keeps apps in memory on purpose, so a low figure is not a problem unless apps keep restarting.
lvi_sclock: The highest current clock among the CPU clusters in this reading. It changes many times a second, so one reading says little on its own; below, the clock of every cluster.
lvi_sload: System load over the last minute: how many tasks were running or waiting - for the CPU or for storage - on average. Android counts storage waits too, so this number alone can read past the core count on a phone that is doing almost nothing; that is normal, not an overload. The percentage beside it is the part of the last seconds the cores were genuinely busy, measured from /proc/stat between two readings. The 5- and 15-minute figures and the per-core share are in the tooltip.
lvi_sbattery: Charge level and voltage, read straight from the battery driver. The voltage falls as the charge goes down and sags briefly under load; below, the battery temperature.
lvi_suptime: Time since the phone was last started. Below, when that was.
lvi_trend_rate: %1 °C per minute over the last %2 s
t_lsp_off: LSPosed verbose log: off after a reboot
t_lsp_already: LSPosed verbose log is already off
t_lsp_restored: LSPosed setting put back · after a reboot
t_lsp_manual: This LSPosed keeps the setting differently - switch Verbose log off in its manager
lv_eta_all_tip: Estimate: this profile has no screen-off hour of its own yet - from the screen-off drain of all profiles together, %s.
learn_tip_profile: Completed sessions of this profile the governor has learned from: %s.
lvi_learner_prof: How many sessions of this profile (“{ses}” on the tile) the governor has learned from. Each records how long the phone took to warm up, how hot it got and how well the ceilings held; the profile’s thresholds adapt from them. On Battery the tile also rates the last session: clean, partial, noisy or disturbed.
lvb_charge_tip: On the charger: the records and the drain learning pause - charge coming in cannot be measured as drain.
lvb_charge_cool_tip: The battery warms on the charger: Smart holds the CPU back to protect it.
lvb_charge_assist_tip: Cool on the charger: Smart allows a little more headroom.
lr_prof_note: Only the minutes each profile was actually active count; charging time is excluded.
lr_aod_fmt: panel lit in {lit} of {of} screen-off checks
lr_tip_awake_who: During idle the phone stayed awake {awake}% of the time - {who} is the main holder.
lr_sm_smart_only: Usage records learn only while the Smart profile is active - this capture ran under a different one.
lr_scr_note: The Monitor tiles measure only calm stretches of an hour or more; these rows cover the whole capture - different windows, both figures are right.
lr_ph_note: Every stretch of the day, longest first; a plus is charge gained on the charger.
lr_wlt_head: Most frequent partial holds (CPU kept awake):
lr_tip_awake_alarm: During idle the phone stayed awake {awake}% of the time - the most frequent wakeup: {who}.
lr_tip_awake_hold: During idle the phone stayed awake {awake}% of the time - the most frequent holder: {who}.
lr_wake_gap: No holders were recorded even though idle was restless - the counters stayed flat; see the full report for the live samples.
lr_nd_verdict_ok: An excellent night: {pct}%/h with {deep}% deep sleep.
lr_nd_verdict_mid: A decent night, but the {awake}% awake share ate part of the gain.
lr_nd_verdict_bad: An expensive night: {pct}%/h - see the holders above and the advice below.
lr_tip_prof_save: Your own measurements: {cheap} cost {x}%/h at the screen against {y}%/h on {busy} - for reading and music it is noticeably cheaper.
lr_tip_heat_warm: The CPU held 45 °C+ for {min} (hottest: {phase}) - sustained heat costs battery and comfort.
lr_tip_heat_warm_set: The CPU held 45 °C+ for {min} (hottest: {phase}) - "{set}" in Settings is on Stock, so the protection kicks in later than it could.
lr_tip_heat_calm: The phone stayed cool all day (peak {cpu} °C) and never throttled - nothing to change.
stock_load_busy: CPU actually busy: %1 % over the last %2 s
